req.title: POST-only actions reject GET
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET requests to /<id>/delete must return HTTP 405. The delete route in blog.py is registered with methods=('POST',) only, so Flask will automatically return 405 for GET. Tests cover: (1) positive — GET on a valid post id returns exactly 405; (2) negative — POST on the same endpoint (with auth) succeeds with 302, confirming POST is allowed; (3) boundary — GET on id=0 (non-existent boundary) still returns 405 (method check precedes resource lookup); (4) additional boundary — GET on id=1 (the exact fixture post id) returns 405, not 404 or 200. This suite kills mutations that change the status code constant, flip the method restriction, or alter the route methods tuple.

tests.name: test_get_delete_returns_405_for_valid_post_id
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 405
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_returns_405_for_valid_post_id():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_get_delete_returns_405_for_valid_post_id()

tests.name: test_post_delete_with_auth_returns_302_not_405
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database contains post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username=test)
Client is authenticated as user test
expected: DELETE POST request returns HTTP 302 (redirect to index), NOT 405
trace: R-FLASKR-030: POST must be allowed on /<id>/delete (only GET is rejected with 405)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_post_delete_with_auth_returns_302_not_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 405

test_post_delete_with_auth_returns_302_not_405()
